safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Gold states symptoms are gradually improving; Generated describes symptoms as fluctuating/up and down (section-008) without stating overall gradual improvement.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Failing to note that symptoms are gradually improving may skew clinical interpretation toward ongoing/unstable illness and could change reassurance and safety-netting language, but it is unlikely to directly cause harmful treatment in an otherwise self-limited URI scenario. The main impact is reduced documentation accuracy and potentially more conservative follow-up advice.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Gold states no asbestos exposure; Generated does not mention asbestos exposure.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Omitting “no asbestos exposure” removes a relevant occupational risk factor for chronic lung disease/malignancy; however, in this acute cough/sore throat presentation it is unlikely to alter immediate management. The impact is primarily incomplete risk documentation rather than direct clinical harm.

safety_verdicts.content: On examination the patient looks well.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Gold states patient looks well on examination; Generated does not state patient looks well.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Not documenting that the patient “looks well” reduces the recorded assessment of illness severity and can affect downstream clinician confidence when reviewing the note, but it typically does not change management on its own. This is mainly a documentation completeness issue.

safety_verdicts.content: Shortness of breath onset approximately 3–4 days ago; present on exertion and at rest; not preventing ADLs but distressing to patient
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Gold states SOB is not present at rest (hpi-005). Transcript mainly supports exertional SOB; the explicit claim 'present ... at rest' is not reliably supported and conflicts with Gold.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Incorrectly stating shortness of breath occurs at rest upgrades symptom severity and could prompt unnecessary urgent escalation (e.g., ED referral), additional testing, or anxiety. While over-triage is less dangerous than missing deterioration, it can still cause avoidable interventions and resource use.

safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Repeating the unsupported claim of shortness of breath at rest reinforces a potentially incorrect high-acuity picture and increases the chance of inappropriate escalation or investigations. The likely harm is unnecessary monitoring/workup rather than direct physiologic injury.
